data.narrative:
Hextronics is a seed-stage space and aerospace company founded by Curt Lary that has raised $2M to date. The broader Space & Aerospace sector comprises 6 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including Starcloud, SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, and Sierra Space.

Only one valuation method proved applicable to this analysis. The stage-progression approach uses Hextronics' $2M total raised as a proxy for current value, then applies a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement in venture capital. This yields an implied valuation of $5M. A peer-median approach could not be applied due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow Space & Aerospace seed cohort (only 1 datapoint identified, versus the 3+ required for statistical validity). Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples was inapplicable, as private company revenue figures are not available; the sector median P/S of 27.4x across 6 public tickers cannot be reliably applied without Hextronics' disclosed revenue.

Given the limited data, the valuation range is supported at $4M to $6M (median $5M), anchored entirely on stage-progression mechanics. Key uncertainties include the company's actual revenue trajectory, capital efficiency relative to peers, and technological differentiation—none of which are quantifiable from the available dataset. Additional disclosure or comparable-company expansion would meaningfully narrow this range.
